summary: MarsWalk is a web application that assists Mars Astronauts in making a safe spacewalk. It was created on an actual location which is the ridges on Mount Sharp in the Gale crater where the Curiosity rover operated in 2025. The astronaut selects a scientific target he or she wants to go to, and MarsWalk then determines the path of walking over the HiRISE terrain which is least dangerous. It is able to display the time, oxygen, radiation, temperature, and daylight. There is also a solar storm drill in case of one happens during their journey to the location, and it is able to tell them the time it takes them to get to a shelter. It got information from three NASA missions at a walking scale. We looked at our planner and compared it to the actual data of Curiosity when it drove there, and every number has been cited or labelled. There are also maps of Mars to show the terrain of it and how it might look outside of the research area. MarsWalk is able to take the data from NASA and use it to make decisions that can keep the crew safe and help them discover new scientific data and conduct more experiments.
details:
LIVE APP URL: https://scopemint.github.io/marswalk/

You can also access the app by following the instructions in the README in Github.

WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS:

MarsWalk transforms multi-layered NASA information into the decisions that a suited astronaut would need to make on a Marswalk: where to go, how long it will take, how much it will cost the suit, and when to come back.

Challenge's own example science goal – Site: 4 km x 4 km box on Curiosity's actual traverse to the 2025-26 boxwork on Mount Sharp, Gale Crater (4.81°S, 137.37°E). The three locations mentioned are where Curiosity actually landed: Altadena (sol 4571), the Monte Grande hollow / Nevado Sajama ridge pair (sols ~4695-4718), the boxwork entry (sol 4548), and the current location of Curiosity (sol 5073). One is a boxwork field that we spotted in HiRISE images, but which no rover has visited yet.

When you select a target, MarsWalk:

(1) walks through 10m resolution (1,600,000 terrain cells) Digital Terrain Model generated from HiRISE 1 m data. It prevents going up slopes when the crew exceeds their limits, and slows on uphill and rocky surfaces. It takes ~0.1s to run in a Web Worker.

(2) Calculates walk back time from all points on the route and point of no return.

(3) simulates a walking pair of buddies using a suit model and a walking energy model from Pandolf (1977) scaled to Mars gravity, oxygen from Weir (1949), CO2 and cooling water of the suit capacity.

(4) Shows radiation (Curiosity RAD: 210 ± 40 μGy/day, Hassler et al. 2014; the largest storm RAD measured was 8,100 μGy on 20 May 2024), air temperature (real hourly REMS data for today's Mars season) and daylight (live Mars24 clock: sol, local Mars time, sunrise, sunset). It then provides GO/NO-GO slope, daylight and time budget (25% reserve).

Prints an EVA cue card containing: elapsed time, local time, stations, oxygen remaining and turn-back rule.

(6) Playback the walk in a full screen helmet visor HUD, a 3D HiRise terrain view and a first-person walk.

(7) Provides the crew with the actual image of each target taken by Curiosity, to help them know what they are looking for.

(8) Computes multi-stop traverses: measures time on actual terrain and selects fastest visiting sequence.

(9) Identify hazards: radio line of sight shadows (calculated over terrain), rocky ground and near slope limits. The crew can move the base and also select any point where they can draw "no-go" zones that the route will not pass.

(10) Rover check: performs 19 legs of Curiosity with our planner and tests each leg at 15, 20 and 25 degrees. If the legs are connected then they are green, if they can't be connected they are red.

(11) "Why not walk straight?": displays the straight line next to the safe route, and the too steep portions in red, indicating the % detour.

(12) Pages: Plan route, Map layers, Weather, Solar storms, Summary. Ground temperature, air pressure and UV for the current Mars month from 4,745 sols of REMS reports are added as weather. Solar storms display real storms that Curiosity measured, as well as a storm drill. For radiation and temperature, there is a range of the measurement being shown not a single number.

It installs as an application, and is completely offline as Mars doesn't have internet.

BENEFIT AND IMPACT INTENDED:

The tools used to map Mars today (USGS geologic maps, JPL Mars Trek) are designed to provide regional to global perspectives. MarsWalk operates on the level of an individual “Mars-walking” man or woman in a suit. By simply varying the study box, it provides a concrete prototype that can be re-run for any HiRISE terrain model for any site. It brings a Mars walk to life and to the public and classroom for educators. Each of the numbers is described as an assumption—the honesty that is required for a real mission plan.

HOW IT IS CREATIVE:

Most Mars data tools are used to visualise the location of things. MarsWalk demonstrates the possibility of a crew to do about it. It's a novelty, a combination of slope-aware routing, suit consumables, a live mars clock, radiation and temperature ranges from the real mission, and checking against a real rover's drive, all in the same spot on the same terrain.
